feedback.problem:
Determine if $v=[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 \\ -8 & 4\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
feedback.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors are non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 4 \\ -8 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4-4\text{i} \\ -8\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4{\text{i}}^{2}-4\text{i} \\ -8\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =-4\text{i}[\begin{aligned}1+\text{i} \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =-4\text{i}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=-4\text{i}v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =-4\text{i}.$
